campaign.days: Days 4 to 20: the Long Winter and Fimbulwinter.
decree.d4: Freyja has claimed her share of the slain. Each day she names a whim; the worthy who match it go to Fólkvangr.
decree.d5: A sea battle. The drowned belong to Rán, whatever they tell you.
whim.amber: Freyja claims whoever wears amber today.
shop.sundial.text: Skögul teaches you to read the sun. Each shift gets 30 more seconds.
decree.d6: Odin decrees: outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel, whatever else is true. Search the registry when you have cause to.
rule.outlaw: Outlaws and oathbreakers named in the registry go to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.registry: If the registry names this soul (same name, same hair), they are an outlaw.
law.unregistered: If the registry has nobody by that name, or only someone else who shares it, they are not.
cue.brokenRing: A broken oath-ring on a thong
tm.oath.kept.1: I never broke an oath in my life. Ask anyone.
tm.oath.kept.2: My word is iron. Every oath I swore, I kept.
tm.oath.kept.3: I kept faith with my jarl to the end.
q.oath.confess.1: …All right. I swore on the ring and ran when it counted. The clerks wrote it down, didn't they.
q.oath.confess.2: It was one oath. One. And the jarl deserved it.
q.oath.excuse.1: Oaths are complicated. I'd rather not say more.
rv.huginn.outlaw: Huginn saw {name} break an oath sworn on the ring.
case.geir.knows: You know me. I sat at your father's table every winter.
case.geir.plea: Whatever the clerks wrote down, it was a long time ago.
decree.d7: Odin decrees: only a warrior's own weapon counts. Whoever fell with a borrowed blade goes to Hel. You may use the rune-lens.
decree.d8: Odin decrees, against Naglfar: clip every soul's untrimmed nails before you send it on, whatever its stamp.
rule.borrowed: A soul who fell holding someone else's weapon goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
law.ownBlade: If the owner's runes name the soul ("…á mik", "…owns me"), the weapon is theirs.
law.borrowedBlade: If the owner's runes name someone else, the weapon was borrowed or taken.
law.copyUlfberht: A copy puts the cross at the end: +VLFBERHT+.
cue.wrongGrip: The grip is wrapped for a bigger hand
proc.clip: Clip untrimmed nails before sending a soul on (Naglfar decree).
obs.inscription.own: Owner's runes: "{name} á mik" ({name} owns me)
obs.inscription.other: Owner's runes: "{other} á mik" ({other} owns me)
tm.owner.self.1: This was my father's axe, and his father's before him.
tm.owner.self.2: Nobody else has ever held this blade. Nobody would dare.
tm.blade.ulfberht.1: My sword was a true Ulfberht. You can read it on the blade.
tm.blade.ulfberht.2: A true Ulfberht, bought in Hedeby for a year's silver.
q.owner.confess.1: …It was my brother's. Mine broke in the first rush. He wasn't using it; he was already dead.
q.blade.confess.1: The merchant swore it was real. I suppose he would.
decree.d11: Odin decrees: a soul's saga tally is evidence, unless it's forged. Under the rune-lens a forgery gives itself away (a rune from the old alphabet, a rune carved backwards, or a garbled carver's line). Ignore a forged tally entirely.
cue.freshCarving: A tally stick in the belt, its cuts fresh and pale
tell.elderRune: Under the lens: one rune, ᛗ, belongs to the old alphabet that carvers stopped using centuries ago.
tell.mirroredRune: Under the lens: one rune is carved backwards, the way a copier gets it wrong.
tell.brokenFormula: Under the lens: the carver's closing line is garbled ("reist mik" where it should say "reist rúnar").
tl.cause.sickness: Died of a fever in the winter.
tl.cause.oldAge: Died old, in bed, among grandchildren.
tl.fled.false: Never turned from the shield wall.
tl.fled.true: Turned and ran at the last.
tl.owner.self: Carried the family's weapon and no other.
tl.outlaw.false: Kept every oath sworn on the ring.
q.tally.confess.1: …I paid a carver in Ribe. Everybody does it. Well. Everybody who can afford it.
q.tally.confess.2: My brother carved it. He meant well. He can't spell either.
q.tally.excuse.1: I can't read. I just carried the stick they gave me.
decree.d10: Odin decrees, with the clerk of the White Christ reading over his shoulder: the baptized belong to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER. The prime-signed, who took the sign of the cross but never the water, are still ours.
decree.d12: Odin decrees: Loki is walking among the dead in borrowed faces. The dwarf Brokkr once sewed his lips shut, and the scars never faded. Whoever bears them, stamp DETAIN.
rule.transfer: The baptized belong to the clerk of the White Christ. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.detain: Loki, in whatever face he wears, is held for Odin. Stamp DETAIN.
law.cross: A cross at the neck means they took the water: baptized.
law.primeSigned: A hammer and a cross on one cord means prime-signed: the sign of the cross, never the water. Still ours.
law.hammer: Thor's hammer at the neck means they never took the water.
law.stitchedLips: Stitch scars across the lips mean Loki.
law.plainLips: Lips without scars mean it isn't Loki.
obs.amulet.hammerAndCross: A hammer and a cross on one cord
obs.lipScars.stitched: Small stitch scars across the lips
tm.creed.heathen.1: I kept to the old gods. Never took the water.
tm.creed.heathen.2: Thor's man, born and buried. Put that on your slate.
tm.creed.baptized.1: I was washed in the White Christ's water at Hedeby. It was very cold.
tm.creed.baptized.2: I'm a Christian, me. Baptized and everything. Is the clerk's hall warm?
tm.creed.primeSigned.1: I took the sign of the cross to trade in York. Nobody put me in any water.
tm.guise.1: Just a plain man, me. Nothing up my sleeves.
tm.guise.2: Honest as the day is long. And the days are getting long, aren't they?
q.creed.hid.confess.1: ...All right, I was washed. My wife made me. Don't tell Odin.
q.creed.claimed.confess.1: The hammer? A gift. A joke. ...Fine. I never saw a priest in my life.
q.creed.excuse.1: It's complicated. There was a river, and some singing, and I may have fallen in.
q.guise.deflect.1: Ask me something harder. You know you want to.
q.guise.deflect.2: What a clever question. Clever enough to get you into trouble. Next.
rv.huginn.baptized: Huginn: Saw this one dunked in a river by a man in a long robe. Twice, to be sure.
rv.huginn.primeSigned: Huginn: Took the sign of the cross at a market. Never the water. Kept the hammer too.
case.loki12.nails: You've been biting your nails. Don't. Somebody needs them.
case.loki12.again: We've met, haven't we? No. I'd remember a face like yours. I collect them.
ending.sliceEnd.title: The slice ends here
ending.sliceEnd.text: Twelve days at the gate. Loki walks among the dead, your brother is building a ship in the north, and Ragnarök is eight days away. The full game tells the rest.
rv.muninn.oathBroken: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Swore on the temple ring, then sold the jarl out for silver. I remember.
rv.muninn.oathKept: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Kept every oath. Every one. I remember because it was so rare.
rv.muninn.heathen: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Never went near the water. Sacrificed at Uppsala every ninth year.
rv.muninn.baptized: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Walked into a river after a man in a long robe. Came out a Christian.
rv.muninn.primeSigned: Muninn: {name} {patronym}. Took the sign of the cross to trade at an English market. Never the water.
rv.muninn.ownWeapon: Muninn: That weapon was {name}'s own. Paid for with a summer's raiding.
rv.muninn.borrowedWeapon: Muninn: That weapon isn't {name}'s. Lifted from a dead man's hand.
decree.d9: No new decree. Odin's ring Draupnir drips tonight, eight rings for the chooser. Work well until then.
decree.d13: Odin decrees: both ravens will speak. Huginn saw how they died; Muninn remembers how they lived. They never lie, but they may seem to disagree. When they do, the Order of Judgment decides. And Muninn forgets more every day.
decree.d14: Hel sends word: her hall is full. Until she has room, those who died in their beds, of sickness or old age, go to the clerk, who says he has plenty. Everyone else Hel takes as before.
decree.d15: Odin decrees: he names his own claim each day, as Freyja does. When both of them want a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins and the soul goes to Valhalla. A blade with no maker's mark is plain: no Ulfberht.
rule.helFull: While Hel's hall is full, straw deaths (sickness, old age) that no earlier rule claims go to the clerk. Stamp TRANSFER.
rule.odinClaim: When Freyja's whim and Odin's claim both fit a worthy soul, Odin's claim wins. Stamp VALHALLA.
whim.odin.scarred: Odin claims the scarred today: two or more wounds in front.
whim.odin.ulfberht: Odin claims whoever carries a true Ulfberht today.
law.noMark: A blade with no maker's mark is a plain blade, not an Ulfberht.
decree.d16: Odin decrees: liars forfeit the halls of the worthy. A soul that would go to Valhalla or Fólkvangr but is caught in a lie, aloud or on a forged tally, goes to Hel. Catch every lie. Until you do, a soul is honest.
decree.d17: Odin decrees: those who died in their beds but were marked with a spear point before death are his, as he once marked himself. Look for the mark over the heart. Liars still forfeit it.
rule.liars: A soul the halls of the worthy would take, caught in a lie (aloud or on a forged tally), goes to Hel. Stamp HEL.
rule.spearMark: A soul marked with a spear point before death is Odin's, even if they died in bed. Stamp VALHALLA.
obs.spearMark.true: A spear point's cut over the heart, made before death
q.blade.plain.confess.1: All right, it's a plain blade. A good plain blade. It killed people just the same.
decree.d18: No new decree. Draupnir drips tonight, for the last time. In the north they say Naglfar is nearly built.
decree.d19: No new decree. Every rule stands. Tomorrow the wolf is loose, so judge well tonight: every soul you send fights for someone.
decree.d20: Ragnarök. Heimdall has blown the horn and the dead are coming all at once. Every rule stands. Judge as many as you can before the sun goes out.
shop.registryIndex.text: Skögul's tabs on the registry's edge. Searching it takes 2 seconds less.
shop.lensPolish.text: A cloth and a jar of fat for the rune-lens. Reading runes takes half the time.
shop.whetstone.text: Keeps the clippers keen. Clipping takes 2 seconds less.
shop.hornOfBrass.text: A louder question gets a quicker answer. Questioning costs 10 seconds instead of 20.
shop.waterClock.text: Measures the sun's last hour exactly, so none of it is wasted. Each shift gets 60 more seconds.
ending.naglfar.title: Naglfar sails early
ending.naglfar.text: You left the nails long and took Loki's bargain. The ship of dead men's nails leaves the north two days before the gods are ready. Loki keeps his word to you, in his way: your family is aboard, and so are you. DRAFT.
ending.rebirth.title: The green earth
ending.rebirth.text: You learned what Odin knew and chose anyway. The host you sent holds long enough. After the fire, a new earth rises from the sea, green and unsown, and among the few who walk out onto it are the people you kept alive. DRAFT.
ending.smuggled.title: Smuggled home
ending.smuggled.text: The ferryman takes your rings and asks nothing. While the gods look the other way, your family crosses to a shore the wolf will never reach. You go back to the gate alone. Someone has to. DRAFT.
ending.transfer.title: The transfer
ending.transfer.text: The clerk's contract was generous and full of small print. When the horn blows, you are reassigned to a warmer office in another department, with a pension. DRAFT.
ending.hel.title: Hel's steward
ending.hel.text: Hel remembers who filled her hall when the gods wanted only heroes. After the fire, she makes you steward of the quiet dead, and you are good at it. DRAFT.
ending.freyja.title: Freyja's own
ending.freyja.text: You gave Freyja the souls she wanted, whatever Odin said. At Ragnarök her field holds, and she takes you in among the chosen, the way Valkyries once were. DRAFT.
ending.odin.title: Chooser eternal
ending.odin.text: Odin's hall was full and the host was strong. He falls to the wolf anyway, as foretold, but not before he names you chooser for whatever world comes next. DRAFT.
ending.wolf.title: The wolf wins
ending.wolf.text: Too few worthy dead, too many who ran, and Naglfar full to the rails. The gods fall quickly. From the gate you watch the fire come. DRAFT.
ending.lastStand.title: The last stand
ending.lastStand.text: Twenty days at the gate. The host you chose fights, and falls, as the gods do. What comes after is not yours to judge. DRAFT.
